 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 13, 2026, 07:57:17 IST SUMMARY India vs New Zealand Live Score, 4th ODI: The India vs New Zealand fourth ODI promises an intriguing contest as the two sides meet at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday, November 13. After rain disrupted the third ODI in Hamilton, both teams will be hoping for a full match, with clear weather forecast for the fourth encounter. 
 India head into the contest with the series advantage and cannot lose the ODI series following the Hamilton washout. New Zealand, meanwhile, will be aiming to win the remaining matches and force a series draw. The match also presents an opportunity for both teams to assess their combinations ahead of their respective international commitments. 
 India will have a different look, with Shreyas Iyer taking charge as captain. Shubman Gill, KL Rahul and Anshul Kamboj have joined the Test squad preparations, leaving several spots open in the playing XI. Ishan Kishan is likely to open alongside Rohit Sharma, while Ruturaj Gaikwad and Tilak Varma are competing for a middle-order opportunity. Mohammed Siraj could also feature after missing the recent matches. 
 New Zealand have brought in Finn Allen, Mitch Hay, Dean Foxcroft and Brett Randell following several departures from the ODI squad. Matt Henry is in contention to return after recovering from a head injury and a quadriceps issue. Blair Tickner, however, remains unavailable. 
 Bay Oval has generally produced conditions that can assist bowlers, with the last 300-plus total at the venue coming in February 2020. India's impressive top-order numbers since the 2023 World Cup will be tested against a New Zealand side that has traditionally been difficult to beat at home. 
 Can Shreyas Iyer lead India's new-look combination to another victory, or will New Zealand keep their hopes of drawing the series alive? Follow all the build-up, team news, probable XIs and key talking points from the fourth ODI. Commentary

 07:28 (IST) Nov 13 Right, after a rain-soaked first half of this ODI series, we are finally set for a full game of cricket. The weather is pleasant, with a light breeze blowing across the ground, and the Bay Oval is almost at full capacity, creating a beautiful atmosphere. The two umpires make their way to the middle. Right behind them, Shreyas Iyer leads the Indian team out of the huddle as the players disperse and take up their respective fielding positions. Will Young and Tim Seifert are the two openers for New Zealand, with Young taking the strike. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball and is raring to go. A slip in place and 'Let's Play', commands the umpire. Here we go...

 07:07 (IST) Nov 13 India vs New Zealand 4th ODI Live Score: TOSS India captain Shreyas Iyer opts to field vs New Zealand in Mount Maunganui 07:05 (IST) Nov 13 The skipper of New Zealand - Mitchell Santner has a smile on his face and jokes that he won't be heading to the casino anytime soon. He reckons it should be a good day for cricket, with pace and bounce expected from the surface. Santner informs that they have made 6 changes to the side, with Bracewell, Foxcroft, Allen, Clarke and Henry coming into the XI. He feels this will be a good test of their squad depth against a strong Indian team, especially given the demands of the schedule.
 07:04 (IST) Nov 13 The captain of India - Shreyas Iyer says that when he looked at the wicket yesterday, there was a bit of grass, but notes that it is a bit dry right now and, with dew expected to come, bowling was an obvious choice. He adds that it is important to analyse the matches played so far, although they have not had the opportunity to play complete games. He praises the team's approach and attitude, saying they are treating this game as a knockout and that the next two matches are extremely important. Regarding the team changes, he says Ruturaj Gaikwad, Ishan Kishan, and Kuldeep Yadav are making their way into the XI for this game.
 06:45 (IST) Nov 13 India vs New Zealand 4th ODI Live Score: India are in a strong position India are in a strong position after the third ODI in Hamilton was washed out. They cannot lose the series, while New Zealand can only hope to level it by winning the remaining matches.
 Rain has affected all three matches so far. However, the move to Mount Maunganui brings some hope, with clear weather forecast for the fourth ODI. The city did witness rain a week ago, though.
 06:10 (IST) Nov 13 India vs New Zealand Live Score: Bay Oval conditions, India's batting numbers and New Zealand's home record in focus The fourth ODI between India and New Zealand will bring the teams to Bay Oval, where conditions could once again favour the bowlers. The last time a team crossed the 300-run mark at the venue was in February 2020, when New Zealand scored 300 for 5 in response to India's 296 for 7. India's top three have been particularly impressive since the 2023 World Cup, scoring 4,922 runs at an average of 55.3, including 17 hundreds and 26 fifties. New Zealand's top three average 32.01 in the same period. However, the hosts have not lost a home ODI series since January 2019, also against India. 06:00 (IST) Nov 13 India vs New Zealand Live Score: Ishan Kishan, Ruturaj Gaikwad in focus as India reshuffle batting order India's batting combination will be one of the biggest talking points in the fourth ODI against New Zealand. With Shubman Gill and KL Rahul joining the Test squad preparations, Ishan Kishan is likely to get an opportunity to open alongside Rohit Sharma. The middle order could also see a change, with Ruturaj Gaikwad and Tilak Varma among the options available to India. Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer will be expected to provide stability, while Naman Dhir and Axar Patel could add depth. The new-look combination will be keen to make the most of the opportunities at Bay Oval. 05:50 (IST) Nov 13 India vs New Zealand Live Score: Matt Henry in contention for return as New Zealand make changes New Zealand could welcome Matt Henry back for the fourth ODI against India after the fast bowler recovered from a head injury sustained during a training collision with Devon Conway. Henry has also been working his way back from a low-grade quadriceps tear suffered during the second T20I. His return would strengthen New Zealand's bowling options at Bay Oval. However, Blair Tickner remains unavailable as he serves the ICC's mandatory seven-day stand-down period after being struck by a ball while batting during the second ODI. New Zealand have also added Finn Allen, Mitch Hay, Dean Foxcroft and Brett Randell to their squad. 2 More Updates Load More India vs New Zealand Live Score, 4th ODI: India will look to maintain their unbeaten position in the ODI series when they take on New Zealand in the fourth match at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday. Following the washout in Hamilton, India are in a position where they cannot lose the series, while New Zealand's best possible outcome is to force a draw. With rain affecting all three matches so far, the teams will hope for uninterrupted cricket, with clear weather forecast for the fourth ODI.
The match will mark a fresh beginning for India, with Shreyas Iyer taking over the captaincy in the absence of Shubman Gill. Gill, KL Rahul and Anshul Kamboj have joined India's Test preparations, opening up opportunities for several players. Ishan Kishan is expected to partner Rohit Sharma at the top, while Ruturaj Gaikwad and Tilak Varma are in contention for a place in the middle order. Mohammed Siraj could also return to the playing XI.
New Zealand have made significant changes to their squad, with Finn Allen, Mitch Hay, Dean Foxcroft and Brett Randell joining the group. Several regular players, including Test captain Tom Latham, have left to prepare for the upcoming Test series. Matt Henry could return after recovering from injury, while Blair Tickner remains unavailable.
Bay Oval could offer assistance to the bowlers, with recent ODIs at the venue suggesting that crossing 300 may not be straightforward. India's new-look batting order and New Zealand's revamped combination will be the major talking points as both sides prepare for the fourth ODI.
